<!-- Generated by tools/docgen from doc comments. Do not edit: run scripts/docs.sh. -->

```odin
import graph "fire:graph"
```

Audio graph: nodes connected into a directed acyclic graph, processed once per
audio block on the audio thread and a pool of workers.

Edit the graph on the control thread (`add_node`, `connect`, ...), then
`commit` to compile the edits into a plan the audio thread picks up at its next
block. Call `process` from the audio callback.

```odin
g, _ := graph.create(graph.default_settings(48_000, 512))
defer graph.destroy(g)

osc, _ := graph.add_node(g, dsp.gain_create(), 2, 2)
graph.connect(g, graph.INPUT, 0, osc, 0)
graph.connect(g, graph.INPUT, 1, osc, 1)
graph.connect(g, osc, 0, graph.OUTPUT, 0)
graph.connect(g, osc, 1, graph.OUTPUT, 1)
graph.commit(g)

// in the audio callback:
graph.process(g, &ctx)
```

See /guides/graph/ for a walk-through and /design/graph/ for how it works.

## Constants

### INPUT

```odin
INPUT : Node_Id : Node_Id{0, 1}
```

The graph's audio and event input: the device's input channels, and
incoming events such as MIDI. Connect from it like any node.

### OUTPUT

```odin
OUTPUT : Node_Id : Node_Id{1, 1}
```

The graph's audio and event output: connect into it to reach the device's
output channels and the caller's event writer.

### GRAPH_TAG

```odin
GRAPH_TAG : core.Tag : core.Tag{'G', 'R', 'P', 'H'}
```

Chunk tag of a saved graph: its NODE chunks, then CONN.

### NODE_TAG

```odin
NODE_TAG : core.Tag : core.Tag{'N', 'O', 'D', 'E'}
```

Chunk tag of one saved node: index, type and channels, then PARM and DATA.

### PARAMS_TAG

```odin
PARAMS_TAG : core.Tag : core.Tag{'P', 'A', 'R', 'M'}
```

Chunk tag of a node's saved parameter values.

### DATA_TAG

```odin
DATA_TAG : core.Tag : core.Tag{'D', 'A', 'T', 'A'}
```

Chunk tag of a node's own state; its version is the type's `state_version`.

### CONNECTIONS_TAG

```odin
CONNECTIONS_TAG : core.Tag : core.Tag{'C', 'O', 'N', 'N'}
```

Chunk tag of a graph's saved connections.

### GRAPH_TYPE_ID

```odin
GRAPH_TYPE_ID :: "fire.graph"
```

ID under which nested graphs (`as_node`) are saved.

## Types

### Node_Id

```odin
Node_Id :: struct {
	index: u32,
	generation: u32,
}
```

A node in a graph. Stays valid until the node is removed; a removed node's
ID is rejected rather than reaching another node.

### Settings

```odin
Settings :: struct {
	sample_rate: f64,
	max_block: int,
	input_channels: int,
	output_channels: int,
	workers: int,
	latency_compensation: bool,
	parallel_min_us: f64,
	worker_allocator: mem.Allocator,
	max_events: int,
	max_pending_params: int,
	param_queue: int,
}
```

Graph-wide settings, fixed for the graph's lifetime. Start from
`default_settings`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `sample_rate` |  |
| `max_block` | largest `frames` `process` will be called with |
| `input_channels` | channels on INPUT |
| `output_channels` | channels on OUTPUT |
| `workers` | Worker threads besides the audio thread. -1 = CPU cores − 1; 0 = everything on the audio thread. |
| `latency_compensation` | Delay parallel paths so they arrive aligned (see `latency`). |
| `parallel_min_us` | Run a block on several threads only when the graph has parallel paths and its nodes take more than this much CPU per block (measured as it runs). Below it, waking workers costs more than it saves. 0 = always when there are parallel paths. |
| `worker_allocator` | Installed as context.allocator on worker threads. Nodes must not allocate while processing; the default (zero) is the nil allocator, so an allocation fails instead of hitting the heap. Tests install a trapping allocator here. |
| `max_events` | events a node may emit per block (more are dropped and counted) |
| `max_pending_params` | queued parameter changes per node |
| `param_queue` | parameter changes in flight from the control thread |

### Stats

```odin
Stats :: struct {
	events_dropped: u64,
	params_dropped: u64,
	blocks: u64,
}
```

Counters for things the audio thread had to drop instead of allocating.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `events_dropped` | node output events beyond `max_events` |
| `params_dropped` | parameter changes for full or unknown nodes |
| `blocks` |  |

### Graph

```odin
Graph :: struct {...}
```

A graph. Create with `create`; all procs except `process` are control
thread only. Fields are internal.

### Node_Remap

```odin
Node_Remap :: struct {
	saved: u32,
	now: Node_Id,
}
```

A node of a saved graph and the ID it has after `load`.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `saved` | the node's index when saved (`Node_Id.index`) |
| `now` |  |

### Missing_Node

```odin
Missing_Node :: struct {
	id: Node_Id,
	type_id: string,
	err: core.Error,
}
```

A node `load` could not make: kept as a silent placeholder (see
`is_placeholder`) that saves back exactly what was loaded.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `id` |  |
| `type_id` | allocated with the load's allocator |
| `err` | .Unsupported: no such type registered; else the loader's error |

### Load_Result

```odin
Load_Result :: struct {
	nodes: []Node_Remap,
	missing: []Missing_Node,
	allocator: mem.Allocator,
}
```

What `load` did. Free with `load_result_destroy`.

## Procedures

### default_settings

```odin
default_settings :: proc(sample_rate: f64, max_block: int) -> Settings
```

Stereo in and out, latency compensation on, one worker per core but one.

### create

```odin
create :: proc(settings: Settings, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> (g: ^Graph, err: core.Error)
```

Creates a graph with only INPUT and OUTPUT. Starts the worker threads.

### destroy

```odin
destroy :: proc(g: ^Graph)
```

Stops the workers and frees the graph and every node in it. The audio
thread must no longer call `process`.

### add_node

```odin
add_node :: proc(g: ^Graph, node: core.Node, in_channels: int, out_channels: int) -> (Node_Id, core.Error)
```

Adds a node and prepares it for the graph's sample rate and block size with
`in_channels` inputs and `out_channels` outputs. The graph owns the node
from here on (it is destroyed with the graph or by `remove_node`). Takes
effect at the next `commit`.

### remove_node

```odin
remove_node :: proc(g: ^Graph, id: Node_Id) -> core.Error
```

Removes a node and its connections. The node is released and destroyed once
the audio thread has stopped using it (after a later `commit`). Takes
effect at the next `commit`.

### connect

```odin
connect :: proc(g: ^Graph, src: Node_Id, src_channel: int, dst: Node_Id, dst_channel: int) -> core.Error
```

Routes output channel `src_channel` of `src` into input channel
`dst_channel` of `dst`. Several connections into one input channel are
summed. Fails with .Invalid_Argument for unknown nodes or channels, and
.Invalid_State if the connection would create a cycle or already exists.
Takes effect at the next `commit`.

### disconnect

```odin
disconnect :: proc(g: ^Graph, src: Node_Id, src_channel: int, dst: Node_Id, dst_channel: int) -> core.Error
```

Removes a connection made with `connect`. Takes effect at the next `commit`.

### connect_events

```odin
connect_events :: proc(g: ^Graph, src: Node_Id, dst: Node_Id) -> core.Error
```

Routes the events `src` emits (notes, MIDI, parameter values) into `dst`'s
event input. Events from several sources are merged in time order. From
INPUT: the events passed to `process`; into OUTPUT: the caller's event
writer. Takes effect at the next `commit`.

### disconnect_events

```odin
disconnect_events :: proc(g: ^Graph, src: Node_Id, dst: Node_Id) -> core.Error
```

Removes an event connection. Takes effect at the next `commit`.

### commit

```odin
commit :: proc(g: ^Graph) -> core.Error
```

Compiles the current nodes and connections into a plan and hands it to the
audio thread, which switches to it at the start of its next block. Also
frees plans (and removed nodes) the audio thread has finished with.

### collect

```odin
collect :: proc(g: ^Graph)
```

Frees plans the audio thread has retired, and nodes removed since. `commit`
does this too; call it after removing nodes if no commit follows soon.

### set_param

```odin
set_param :: proc(g: ^Graph, id: Node_Id, param: core.Param_Id, value: f64, at: i64 = 0) -> core.Error
```

Changes a parameter of a node, sample-accurately: the node receives a
`core.Param_Value` event at `at`, a time on the graph's clock (frames since
the graph started processing, see `time`). `at = 0` or a time already past
means the start of the next block. Control thread only (one producer).

### set_param_ramp

```odin
set_param_ramp :: proc(g: ^Graph, id: Node_Id, param: core.Param_Id, target: f64, frames: int, at: i64 = 0) -> core.Error
```

Moves a parameter in a straight line to `target` over `frames` frames,
starting at `at` (as in `set_param`): the node receives a
`core.Param_Ramp`, which it follows exactly instead of smoothing. For
timed fades and glides. Control thread only.

### get_node

```odin
get_node :: proc(g: ^Graph, id: Node_Id) -> ^core.Node
```

The node behind an ID, for reading its state or calling its own API from
the control thread. Nil for unknown IDs, INPUT and OUTPUT.

### latency

```odin
latency :: proc(g: ^Graph) -> int
```

Frames by which OUTPUT lags INPUT after latency compensation, as of the
last `commit`.

### input_latency

```odin
input_latency :: proc(g: ^Graph, id: Node_Id) -> int
```

Frames by which node `id`'s input lags INPUT after latency compensation
(the latency of everything upstream of it), as of the last `commit`: what
a recorder fed from inside the graph is moved earlier by. 0 for unknown
IDs and INPUT; OUTPUT's is `latency`.

### time

```odin
time :: proc "contextless"(g: ^Graph) -> i64
```

The graph's clock: frames processed since the first `process` call. Read on
the control thread it is approximate (the audio thread may be mid-block).

### stats

```odin
stats :: proc "contextless"(g: ^Graph) -> Stats
```

Counters for events and parameter changes the audio thread dropped.

### as_node

```odin
as_node :: proc(g: ^Graph) -> core.Node
```

Wraps a graph as a `core.Node`, so a whole graph can be nested inside
another graph or rendered by `testkit.render`. The node owns the graph:
destroying the node destroys the graph. Its inputs and outputs are INPUT's
and OUTPUT's channels; preparing it with any other sample rate, channel
counts or a larger block fails with .Invalid_Argument.

```odin
inner, _ := graph.create(settings)
// ... build `inner` and commit ...
id, _ := graph.add_node(outer, graph.as_node(inner), 2, 2)
```

### process

```odin
process :: proc(g: ^Graph, ctx: ^core.Process_Context)
```

**Realtime-safe** (callable on the audio thread). Processes one block: `ctx.inputs` feed INPUT, OUTPUT's inputs are
written to `ctx.outputs`, `ctx.events_in` feed INPUT's events and OUTPUT's
events go to `ctx.events_out` (if set). `ctx.frames` may be anything from 0
to `max_block`. Call from the audio thread only; never allocates.

Wire it into a device callback:

```odin
process :: proc(user: rawptr, b: ^backend.Io_Block) {
	ctx := core.Process_Context{inputs = b.inputs, outputs = b.outputs, frames = b.frames}
	graph.process((^graph.Graph)(user), &ctx)
}
```

### load_result_destroy

```odin
load_result_destroy :: proc(r: ^Load_Result)
```

Frees what `load` returned.

### remap

```odin
remap :: proc(r: Load_Result, saved: u32) -> (Node_Id, bool)
```

The ID a saved node has after loading, from `r.nodes`.

### save

```odin
save :: proc(g: ^Graph, w: ^core.State_Writer, ctx: ^core.Save_Context) -> core.Error
```

Control thread. Writes the graph as a GRAPH_TAG chunk: every node (its
type, channel counts, parameter values and own state) and every
connection. Parameter values are the last ones `set_param` or
`set_param_ramp` set; parameters never set are not saved, so they start
as a freshly made node of the type has them. Values that automation or
modulation moves are saved as their base. Fails with `.Unsupported` if a
node's type cannot be saved (no `type_id`), or with the node's own error;
the writer then holds a partial chunk, so discard it.

### load

```odin
load :: proc(g: ^Graph, c: core.Chunk, ctx: ^core.Load_Context, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator, commit_now: bool = true) -> (result: Load_Result, err: core.Error)
```

Control thread. Adds the nodes and connections of a GRAPH_TAG chunk to
`g` (usually empty but for INPUT and OUTPUT) and commits them all at once,
so a running graph switches in one block. Node types come from
`ctx.registry`; a node whose type is not registered, or whose loader
fails, becomes a silent placeholder that keeps its saved state (listed in
`Load_Result.missing`). Loaded nodes start at their saved parameter
values without smoothing. Connections to channels a graph lacks are
skipped. With `commit_now` false, the caller commits (to make other edits
in the same switch). On failure nothing loaded stays in the graph.
`.Invalid_Data` for a malformed chunk.

### nodes

```odin
nodes :: proc(g: ^Graph, allocator: mem.Allocator = context.allocator) -> []Node_Id
```

The nodes in the graph (not INPUT and OUTPUT), in index order. Control
thread; the slice is allocated with `allocator`.

### is_placeholder

```odin
is_placeholder :: proc(g: ^Graph, id: Node_Id) -> bool
```

Whether `id` is a placeholder for a node `load` could not make.

### register_types

```odin
register_types :: proc(reg: ^core.Node_Registry) -> core.Error
```

Registers the node types this package provides (nested graphs, as made
by `as_node`), so saved state can name them.
